text.p: Italian bonds ended slightly higher on the day playing catch-up with Btp futures after taking a one day holiday on Thursday.
LIFFE futures themselves fell in a bout of retracement following the previous day's gains when the domestic cash market was closed.
"The market's really quiet today, there are few institutions in," one London based broker said.
The lira was holding around its central ERM parity level of 990 against the mark, softer on early session levels.

The February 2007 Btp ended 19 basis points higher at 95.27 with a yield of 7.56 percent and a spread over the benchmark Bund of 182 basis points. The June LIFFE future was 29 basis points easier at 127.96.
Many domestic players are absent from the market, extending Thursday's one day public holiday into the weekend, so trade was thin and activity low.

U.S. jobs data were slightly softer than expected but had little impact on Btps. On the home front, players were speculating over the chances of a discount rate cut from the Bank of Italy, which traders said was partially discounted.

Some traders said the next window of opportunity for a possible cut in Italy's 6.75 percent discount rate was Tuesday when the final consumer price figure for April, forecast at 1.7 percent year on year from March's 2.2 percent, is due to be released.
But traders were divided over the likelihood of a cut with some seeing the possibility of one next week and others favouring the end of this month.
